name: InWove integration protocol
about: The knobs of the method, as data. A change to the method is a change to this file, in the same pull request as the rule in PROTOCOL.md it carries. Every knob has a reason beside it; when the reason stops holding, change or remove the knob.

slice_max_mb.why: A reader given more starts skimming. In the run, slices of 0.4 to 2.4 MB were used; a 2.2 MB slice came back partial and several slices near 2 MB needed a second reader for their last files. Lower it if your readers come back partial.

resplit_mb.why: The size a slice is cut to when it came back partial. Three parts of 0.6 to 0.8 MB each finished cleanly in the run.

readers_at_once.why: The ceiling of the tool that launched the agents in the run. Nothing else. Set it to your own tool's ceiling.

report_every.why: A reader's context will be cut on a slice this size. What it appended to its report is what is left after the cut.

skip_dirs.why: Installed or built output, not authored. Nobody wrote it by hand, so nobody needs to read it.

binary_sniff_bytes.why: A file with a zero byte in its first 8 KB is treated as binary and listed, not read. Text files do not hold zero bytes.

index_only.why: Files listed but not read line by line, each category with its reason. Patterns: one without a slash matches the file name in any folder; one with a slash matches the path from the repository root, and * may cross folders. A source in sources.json can add its own categories.

rules.reason: Changelogs repeat what the code says, often wrongly; licence texts are standard. The licence is still recorded in sources.json.
Generated by a tool. The versions that matter are in the manifest the lockfile was made from, which is read.
Pictures and fonts carry no interface.

helpers_per_lead.why: The lead must read every diff a helper returns. With more at once it stops reading them.

whole_suite_runs_at_once.why: When many test suites ran at the same time in the run, timing tests failed for no reason. The whole suite runs once, alone, by the lead, at the end. Helpers run only the test files they touch.

one_writer_per_files.why: Every agent that writes code has its own worktree and branch, so two agents never overwrite each other and nothing lands without the level above reading it.

new_dependencies.why: A builder that needs a new package stops that part and says which package, which version and why. A dependency is a decision for a person, not a builder.

roles.why: Judgment up, building down. The strongest model coordinates; strong models lead, split and check; smaller models read and build; the smallest check lists. Pushes, anything said to the owner, and anything touching keys or what leaves the project stay at the top.

builder.used_in_the_run: Sonnet; the first door builder ran on the coordinator's model

helper.used_in_the_run: Sonnet for building, Haiku for searching, listing and mechanical checks

security_reviewer.why: Someone who did not write the code answers the shape of any change that widens what the project reaches or holds.

final_message_lines.why: Each final message is read by the level above, which has many to read. The report on disk holds the detail.

commits.stage: exact files only, never everything in the folder
commits.push: only the coordinator, only after the owner says yes and the coordinator read the diff
commits.why: One accountable reader for what goes out. A builder in the run staged every file in its folder; staging exact files keeps each commit to its own work.

phases.name: Frame
phases.done_when: the goal, its done-test, the sources with commits and pins, the target's rules and what is out of scope are written down, and the sources are cloned read-only

phases.name: Read everything
leaves: notes.md: facts that decide the build
phases.done_when: every report's coverage table lists every file in its slice, partial slices are re-split and read again, and the coordinator has written the facts that decide the build

phases.name: Find what is wrong today
leaves: notes.md: what the file says, what the source says, where
phases.done_when: each existing claim about another project in the target is held against a cited source

phases.name: Lay a shared base, then build side by side
leaves: one branch per line of work
phases.done_when: each builder reports what was built, what tests prove, what is not verified, unconfirmed facts, files that need a person, and faults found

phases.name: Write the facts down for everyone
The security loop
leaves: the reviewer's conditions, each as a test
phases.done_when: every difference between the build and the shape the reviewer answered is sent back with its reason, and answered

phases.name: Review what nobody read
phases.done_when: every kept finding has a file, a line, the input that goes wrong and a fix small enough for a helper

phases.name: Bring it together
phases.done_when: the lines are merged in the fixed order on the target's current main and the whole suite passes, run once, alone

phases.name: Sweeping changes once, at a quiet point
leaves: a list of what was kept and why
phases.done_when: words a person reads changed, identifiers a program matches did not

phases.name: Design the rest as briefs
phases.done_when: each unbuilt piece has a brief one smaller-model session can finish

phases.name: Push, on a yes
phases.done_when: each body says what is verified and what is not, and the first run of the checks has been read

phases.name: Live checks and the record
leaves: results where the projects keep them
phases.done_when: each skipped live check has run against a real service, or says what it is waiting for

phases.name: Hand over
phases.done_when: anyone can continue from the plan without asking

gates.must: its coverage table lists every file in its slice

gates.before: a builder relies on an identifier
gates.must: someone opened the upstream file the report cites
the lead read the diff and ran its tests

gates.before: anything that widens what the project reaches or holds is built
gates.must: the security reviewer answered the shape
the owner said yes, and the coordinator read the diff

gates.before: a change to who may do what goes live
gates.must: the project's people, or the owner for a test service, decided

gates.before: something is called working with another project
gates.must: a live check ran against that project's real service
every citation points at a real file and line
